_meta.description: High-impact scope factors for Cost Studio. Multipliers adjust planning bands only — not contractor bids. Default option id should use 1.0 multipliers.

floridaNotes: Wind and energy code can raise envelope, roof, and window costs versus inland U.S. averages.
Insurance and wind-mitigation upgrades often appear after storms or at policy renewal — budget contingency helps.
Coastal access, HOAs, and impact product requirements can add time and soft costs.
Permitting and inspection cycles vary by jurisdiction; phased or occupied remodels cost more in labor coordination.

globalFactors.label: Layout / structural complexity
globalFactors.help: Moving walls, plumbing, or structure raises cost fast.

options.label: Keep layout
options.description: Minimal moves of walls or plumbing

globalFactors.label: Site access & occupancy
globalFactors.help: Occupied homes and tight lots increase labor time.

extraFactors.label: Roof system
extraFactors.help: Tile and premium metal sit well above basic shingles.

education: Florida wind-mitigation and secondary water barriers often matter as much as the visible roof surface.
Stories, pitch, and tear-off layers change labor and disposal costs quickly.
Cabinets and layout moves usually dominate the budget.
Keeping plumbing in place is one of the largest ways to stay toward the low band.
Waterproofing and tile labor often matter more than fixture sticker prices.
Converting a tub to a walk-in shower is a common mid-to-high cost step.
Systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing) can rival finish costs in older Florida homes.
Occupied whole-home work is slower and usually costs more in labor coordination.
Foundation, roof tie-in, and matching exterior materials drive large swings.
Impact glazing and wind design are common Florida cost adders on additions.
True basements are uncommon in much of Florida — lower-level or walkout spaces need strong moisture control.
Egress, ceiling height, and humidity management can constrain finishes.
Moisture barrier and flashing quality protect the structure more than cosmetic cladding alone.
Multi-story access and substrate repairs are frequent mid-to-high drivers.

extraFactors.label: Outdoor package
extraFactors.help: Cooking and enclosure packages move outdoor projects into higher bands.

education: Screen enclosures and outdoor kitchens are common Florida upgrades with their own specialty trades.
Wind design for covers and roofs should be part of planning, not an afterthought.
Custom homes have the widest variance — site, architecture, and finishes dominate.
Impact products, elevation, and coastal requirements can reshape the budget early.
General contracting scopes vary widely — define trades and outcomes before comparing bids.
Unknown conditions once walls open are a common source of change orders.
